data.body:
The full metric-vs-alarm sweep this ticket's last AC asks for — done, so the fix does not have to
start by re-deriving it. Measured live against CloudWatch.

**41 `rebar/host` metrics; 21 alarmed; 20 unalarmed.** The 20 are not equally interesting, and
lumping them together would overstate the problem. Dispositions:

## Genuinely missing — health/liveness booleans with no alarm (the subject of this ticket)

- `gerrit_healthy` — as filed.
- `reviewbot_healthy` — as filed.
- `mem_probe_ok` — a probe-SUCCESS boolean. Same shape as the two above: if the memory probe
  stops working, nothing pages, and the memory gauges beside it simply stop arriving.
- `container_stats_ok` — same shape, for the container-stats collector.

These four are one class: a boolean whose whole purpose is to say "the measurement happened", with
nothing watching it. A dead probe is indistinguishable from a healthy quiet period.

## Worth a deliberate decision, not obviously wrong

- `disk_pressure_persists` — reads as a CONDITION (pressure did not clear after pruning) rather
  than a probe heartbeat. If that is right it is a candidate for its own alarm; if it is an
  activity counter, it belongs in the group below. Decide explicitly.
- `mem_used_percent` / `mem_available_percent` — there is currently **no alarm on memory
  utilisation at all** on this host. `mcp_mem_abort` IS alarmed, so the consequence of exhaustion
  is watched while the approach to it is not. That may be deliberate (abort is the actionable
  event); record the reasoning either way.

## Reasonably unalarmed — raw gauges whose derived sibling IS alarmed

`docker_buildkit_cache_bytes`, `docker_storage_bytes`, `journal_bytes` — each has a
`*_used_percent` sibling carrying the alarm. Alarming both would double-page.

## Reasonably unalarmed — cost/activity telemetry, not health

`review_bot_llm_{input,output,total,cache_read,cache_write}_tokens`, `container_memory_rss_bytes`,
`container_stats_unparsed_rows`, `deploy_deferrals`, `disk_pressure_prunes`, `review_interrupts`
(its `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded` sibling is alarmed).

## A warning for whoever implements this

Do NOT land a guard test asserting "every liveness metric has an alarm" BEFORE or separately from
the alarms themselves. Such a test fails immediately against current `main` — four metrics are
unalarmed right now — and a red gate on `main` blocks every concurrent session. The test and the
terraform must land together, or the test must start scoped to what is already true and be widened
in the same change that widens the alarms.
